obligation: Affiliate notice: Cloud Software (custodian) to Payments and Payroll (data owner)
citation: POL-03 4.3; 16 CFR 314.4(f) (service provider oversight); intercompany agreement (pending, POAM-020)
trigger: Any event that may involve payroll handoff files or other division customer information held in the WCP
deadline: Within 1 hour of the SOC learning of it
notify: Payments and Payroll Qualified Individual (division CISO)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - scenario incident

obligation: Customer notice under the standard DPA
trigger: Security incident affecting customer data in the WCP
deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's designated security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 410 tenants' exports and 6,800 employers' handoff files

obligation: Customer notice under negotiated DPAs (about 1,240 enterprise customers)
trigger: Same, for customers with 48-hour terms
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's designated security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 61 of the affected customers have 48-hour terms

obligation: Bank service provider notification (Cloud Software to bank customers)
trigger: Computer-security incident that materially disrupts or degrades, or is reasonably likely to, covered services to a banking organization customer for 4 or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact at each affected bank; if none, the CEO and CIO (or two individuals of comparable responsibility)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - export service suspended 9 hours for all tenants, including about 420 bank customers
notifying_entity: Cloud Software customer support vice president
clock_starts: Determination that the disruption is or is likely to be 4 hours or more

obligation: Sponsor bank A notice (payroll program)
citation: Sponsor bank A program agreement (incident notice clause)
trigger: Security incident affecting program data or disrupting program services
deadline: Within 24 hours of determination
notify: Sponsor bank A program risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - handoff files are program data; ACH files late for some employers
notifying_entity: Payments and Payroll chief compliance officer

obligation: Sponsor bank B notice (card program)
citation: Sponsor bank B program agreement (incident notice clause)
trigger: Security incident affecting card program data or services
deadline: Within 24 hours of determination
notify: Sponsor bank B program risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (no card data or card program service involved); confirm with the bank as a courtesy
notifying_entity: Payments and Payroll chief compliance officer

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers without authorization (access is presumed to be acquisition without reliable evidence otherwise)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 1.1 million workers' payroll data
notifying_entity: Payments and Payroll (Qualified Individual with counsel)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known to any employee, officer, or other agent (314.4(j)(2))

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice: Cloud Software to customers
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (the WCP) containing Florida residents' personal information
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected customer (covered entity), with all information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida workers in affected tenants

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice: Payments and Payroll to employers
trigger: Same, for payroll data the division processes for employers
deadline: No later than 10 days after determination
notify: Each affected employer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 95,000 Florida workers in the handoff files
notifying_entity: Payments and Payroll chief compliance officer

obligation: Florida notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of Florida residents' personal information (a first name or initial and last name with a Social Security number is a listed element; a bank account number counts only with a required security or access code)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination; 15 more days only with written good cause to the Department; law enforcement delay on written request
notify: Each affected Florida resident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - sent by the group on behalf of customers and employers that agree (501.171(6)(b)); the covered entity stays responsible
notifying_entity: Each customer or employer (covered entity), or the group as agent

obligation: Florida Department of Legal Affairs notice
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida individuals
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for each covered entity with 500 or more affected Floridians
notifying_entity: Each covered entity, or the group as agent

obligation: Florida consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
notifying_entity: Each covered entity, or the group as agent

obligation: Other states: service provider or agent notice to data owners
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Breach of personal information maintained for another business
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Data owners (customers and employers)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - affected individuals in all 50 states

obligation: Other states: notice to individuals, attorneys general or regulators, and consumer reporting agencies
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Breach of state residents' personal information (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state (for example, without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
notifying_entity: Each covered entity, or the group as agent

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General finding)
notify: SEC (public filing to investors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - publicly traded holding company

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 (annual)
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the next Form 10-K
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe processes and any material effects

obligation: Law enforcement report (voluntary)
citation: FBI field office or IC3; supports FTC notice item 314.4(j)(1)(vi) and state law enforcement delay provisions
trigger: Criminal theft of data
deadline: As soon as practical (Day 0 to 1)
notify: FBI or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended

obligation: CISA voluntary report; CIRCIA (not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (when a final rule takes effect)
deadline: Voluntary today; 72 hours proposed (not in effect as of 2026-09-25)
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary only
clock_starts: Not applicable until a final rule is effective

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any extortion or ransom demand
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Conditional - only if a demand is received
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel; board risk committee

obligation: Cyber insurer notice
trigger: Any actual or suspected incident that may lead to a claim
deadline: As soon as practicable under the policy
notify: Insurer claims contact; panel counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: HIPAA business associate notice to hospital clients
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held by Technology Consulting
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, or the shorter BAA term
notify: Each affected hospital client
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (no PHI in the WCP or the export bucket); kept for consulting incidents

obligation: Federal contracting officer report: covered telecommunications
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services (or covered article) identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario; applies to consulting's federal contracts
notifying_entity: Technology Consulting federal contracts compliance officer

obligation: Federal agency clients (FCI)
citation: 48 CFR 52.204-21 (no incident reporting clause); contract terms
trigger: Incident affecting federal contract information
deadline: Per contract terms (52.204-21 itself has no reporting duty)
notify: Contracting officer if the contract requires
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (no FCI in the WCP)
notifying_entity: Technology Consulting federal contracts compliance officer

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the sponsor bank, not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell sponsor bank B (the acquirer) immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Sponsor bank B (the acquirer); Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the sponsor bank. Other brands as the sponsor bank directs
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (no account data in the WCP)

obligation: CPNI breach notification (FCC)
trigger: Breach of CPNI by a telecommunications carrier or interconnected VoIP provider
deadline: No later than 7 business days after reasonable determination
notify: USSS and FBI via the FCC reporting facility; then customers
applies_at_this_tier: Not applicable (the group is not a carrier)
